text:
Spencer Knight is the clear No. 1 in Chicago, and it has been a hard month to be one. The Blackhawks started 4-13-1, he was pulled after six goals in a 9-2 loss at Carolina on Nov. 7, and the club put his longtime partner Arvid Söderblom on waivers the next day, then traded him to the Rangers on Nov. 15, as the Chicago Sun-Times reported. Knight said publicly that the team should be angry at itself for letting that happen. Drew Commesso is the new backup.

His own numbers sit a little below average. He is 5-10-1 with an .882 save rate and has allowed 2.2 goals more than his shots would usually produce (goals saved above expected measures that gap). The workload is real, 16 starts and 467 shots, and on high-danger chances he is at .722 against a league .685. Last season he finished 11.1 goals above expected in 55 games, and Evolving-Hockey had him well above average too, so the track record says this is more about the team in front of him than a goalie who has lost his game.
